paper_metadata.title: Microstructure, mechanical property and Hall-Petch relationship of a light-weight refractory Al0.1CrNbVMo high entropy alloy fabricated by powder metallurgical process

evidence.quote: A light-weight refractory Al0.1CrNbVMo high entropy alloy (HEA) was fabricated by high energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering (SPS).

Al0.1CrNbVMo HEA powders were prepared by the ball milling process for 12 hours with high purity (99.0~99.9%) elemental powders of Al, Cr, Nb, V and Mo. ... The ball milling process was carried out a milling speed of 200 RPM with the ball to powder ratio of 10:1 without process control agent.

After 12 h of milling, the powders were taken out and consolidated by Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS, SPS-515S) at 1200 °C at a pressure of 50 MPa under vacuum. The milled powders were heated to 600 °C within 1 min, and from 600 °C to the 1200 °C, a heating rate of 100 °C min-1 were applied, and followed by 5 min of holding time at 1200 °C.
